name: Acacia disparrima
description: A tree or shrub 3 to 12 m high with grey-green curved phyllodes that flowers in summer and autumn. It grows mainly on the coast of northern New South Wales.

name: Acacia falcata
description: An erect or spreading shrub or small tree, 2 to 5 m, with curved leaf-like phyllodes and pale yellow flower heads from autumn to winter.

name: Acacia linifolia
description: An erect or spreading shrub, 1.5 to 4 m tall, that flowers through the year and grows in dry forest, woodland and heath on sandy or clayey soils.

name: Acacia pulchella
description: A wattle from South Australia and Western Australia, with the variety pulchella naturalised in NSW.

name: Acacia verniciflua
description: A large shrub with yellow ball flowers and sticky, varnished-looking foliage. It tolerates moderate frost and needs good drainage.
care_note: It needs good drainage.

name: Ageratum houstonianum
description: An erect or sprawling herb 30 cm to 1 m tall with blue-mauve flower heads most of the year, native to Mexico. It is a common weed of wasteland and disturbed ground in NSW and Queensland.
care_note: It is a weed of disturbed ground, so avoid planting it.

name: Ajuga australis
description: A spreading perennial herb with soft hairy leaves and spikes of pink, mauve or purple flowers. It suckers vigorously and makes a groundcover.

name: Alchornea ilicifolia
description: A small tree or more often a straggling shrub to 6 m, found in drier rainforest and at the edge of open forest.

name: Alectryon tomentosus
description: A small tree with brownish hairy young growth and paired leaflets that grows in dry and subtropical rainforest.

name: Allocasuarina torulosa
description: A slender tree 5 to 20 m tall with thick corky red-brown bark and drooping branchlets that grows in coastal hills and ranges.

name: Allocasuarina verticillata
description: A conical, weeping evergreen tree whose fine needle-like branchlets make good shade, shelter and screens. It feeds and shelters birds and tolerates heavy frost, drought and coastal sites.

name: Alternanthera denticulata
description: A prostrate annual with stems to 40 cm that root at the nodes and small rounded flower clusters. It is widespread in New South Wales.

name: Amyema preissii
description: A native mistletoe with thin cylindrical leaves that grows on Acacia and occasionally other hosts in forest and woodland.
care_note: It is a parasite on host trees.

name: Amyema quandang
description: A hanging, white-woolly mistletoe that lives on many Acacia species, especially in inland districts, and flowers from May to October. It is a parasite and is not a garden plant.

name: Anredera cordifolia
description: A weedy, long-lived woody twining vine from South America with fleshy heart-shaped leaves and aerial tubers. It smothers other plants and is a Weed of National Significance.
care_note: It is declared in every state and territory except Western Australia, and in NSW it must not be sold; double-bag its tubers and bulbils for disposal.

name: Arctotheca calendula
description: A low, short-lived weed with a rosette of lobed leaves and yellow daisies with dark centres. It forms mats and is common in lawns and pastures.
care_note: Brisbane City Council lists it as Council Pest Vegetation, so please remove it by spraying or digging out.

name: Asclepias curassavica
description: An upright, tender perennial with clusters of orange-red and yellow flowers that butterflies, bees and moths visit. It is a host for monarch caterpillars, but it self-seeds and is weedy in disturbed areas.

toxic.note: Eaten in quantity it can cause vomiting, diarrhoea and weakness, and the milky sap can irritate skin and eyes. Wear gloves and keep it away from pets.

care_note: It self-seeds and is weedy in disturbed areas, and it is frost tender. Cut it back where it does not die down in winter.

name: Asparagus asparagoides
description: A climber with annual stems up to 4 m long that grows from tubers and rhizomes, with small white fragrant flowers and red berries. It smothers native plants and is a Weed of National Significance.
care_note: In South Australia it is a declared plant under the Landscape South Australia Act 2019, and the state asks landholders to control it and report sightings of the Western Cape form. Please do not plant or move it.

name: Asphodelus fistulosus
description: An upright biennial or short-lived perennial weed with hollow, onion-like leaves and a flowering stem to about 80 cm. It invades degraded pastures and bare ground, and livestock avoid it.
care_note: Weeds Australia lists it as a declared weed in the Northern Territory and Tasmania, so please check your state's rules and remove it rather than plant it.

name: Baloskion tetraphyllum
description: A clumping, evergreen rush with feathery tips and bronze flower stems in summer. It suits boggy ground, pond edges and containers.
care_note: In containers or dry spots it needs regular watering and does best in partial to full shade.

name: Banksia attenuata
description: A tree or shrub with tall, slender yellow flower spikes like candles from spring, visited by nectar-feeding birds and insects. It is easy to grow in many home gardens.

name: Banksia sessilis
description: A large shrub or small tree with prickly, holly-like leaves and rounded pale yellow brush flowers in winter to spring. It is rich in nectar and parrots eat its seed.
care_note: It is very susceptible to Phytophthora, so it needs good drainage.

name: Billardiera fusiformis
description: A twining climber that grows in gardens and has naturalised in parts of NSW.

name: Bossiaea cinerea
description: An erect or spreading shrub to about 1 m that flowers in spring and grows in coastal sand heath and sclerophyll forest.

name: Briza maxima
description: An annual grass up to 60 cm tall with nodding spring seed heads, from the Mediterranean region, common in disturbed areas.

name: Callisia repens
description: A creeping herb whose fleshy stems root at the joints and form dense mats, with small leaves that are often spotted purple. It escapes from pots and baskets into bushland.
care_note: It is an environmental weed in south-east Queensland (not declared), so please keep it out of bushland and remove it completely.

name: Callitris columellaris
description: A tree to 10 m or more with spreading or erect branches and green foliage. It grows on coastal sandy soils.

name: Calochlaena dubia
description: A hardy, clumping, low-maintenance fern with lacy fronds that spreads by rhizomes into dense banks. It suits mass planting and poor soils.

name: Carpobrotus rossii
description: A spreading, evergreen succulent groundcover with thick leaves and pink or purple daisy-like flowers. It copes with salt, drought and sandy soil, and is good for dunes and dry banks.
edible: The leaves and ripe fruit are eaten.

name: Casuarina equisetifolia
description: A tree with drooping branchlets, 6 to 35 m tall, found on rocky coastal headlands and less often on back-beach dunes. It is often planted on sand dunes.

name: Catharanthus roseus
description: An erect perennial to about 70 cm with glossy leaves and rose-pink or white flowers for most of the year. It is a widespread tropical weed that is often grown in coastal gardens.
care_note: It is native to Madagascar and has naturalised in some areas.

name: Centella asiatica
description: A creeping perennial herb that roots along its stems and has small rounded leaves, usually found in damp places near the coast. It can spread as a lawn weed in moist spots.

name: Cirsium vulgare
description: A spiny, upright weed that forms a rosette first and then a branched stem with purplish flower heads. It is common on pastures and roadsides.
care_note: Declared in Victoria only; Queensland lists it for information only, so please remove it before it seeds.

name: Convolvulus angustissimus
description: A perennial with trailing and twining stems that flowers from early spring to mid autumn, found in grassy eucalypt woodland on loam and clay soils.

name: Coprosma repens
description: A prostrate shrub to small tree up to 8 m, with glossy broad leaves and orange-red fruit, native to New Zealand. It has naturalised along Australian beaches and coastal headlands.
care_note: It is naturalised on coastal beaches and headlands, so avoid planting it near bushland.

name: Cotula australis
description: A low, spreading herb with finely divided leaves and small pale yellow or cream flower heads. It grows in open grassy areas and is a weed of roadsides and lawns.

name: Cotula coronopifolia
description: A low, slightly fleshy plant with small yellow button flowers that grows in damp, often salty, disturbed ground. It is a South African plant that has naturalised in Australia.

name: Cymbalaria muralis
description: A trailing herb with small ivy-shaped leaves and tiny blue-violet snapdragon-like flowers that grows in wall crevices. It came from Europe and spreads by runners that root at the nodes.
care_note: It is introduced and can spread through walls and moist garden sites.

name: Cymbopogon refractus
description: A tussock-forming perennial grass with arching, lemon-scented leaves and soft flower heads like barbed wire. It is a host plant for several native grass butterflies.

name: Cyperus eragrostis
description: A tufted sedge from South America with umbrella-shaped flower heads, a weed of damp soils, drains, gardens and lawns.
care_note: It is a weed of gardens, lawns and drains; I found no state weed page asking for its removal.

name: Cytisus scoparius
description: A tall, woody weed with bright yellow pea flowers and upright ribbed stems that forms dense thickets. Its seeds and leaves are poisonous.

toxic.note: NSW WeedWise says the seeds and leaves are poisonous and can cause nausea and high blood pressure; call the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26.

care_note: NSW does not allow it to be sold, and it is a declared weed in the ACT, NSW, SA, TAS, VIC and WA, so please remove it rather than plant it.

name: Dianella tasmanica
description: A hardy evergreen perennial with arching strappy leaves up to 1.2 m long, nodding blue to purple star flowers in spring and summer, and glossy deep blue berries.

name: Dicksonia antarctica
description: A tough tree fern with a fibrous trunk and a spreading crown of fronds, reliable in shade. Remove dead fronds once or twice a year and keep the trunk shaded while it establishes.
pruning: Remove dead and dying fronds once or twice a year, and feed with well-rotted manure at the same time.

name: Digitalis purpurea
description: An upright herb with a rosette in its first year and tall spikes of purple, pink or white bell flowers in spring and summer in its second. It escapes from gardens into moist forest, especially in Victoria and Tasmania.

toxic.note: All parts contain digitoxin and can be fatal if eaten, so wear gloves and keep it away from children.

care_note: It is a recognised environmental weed in Victoria and Tasmania, so please do not let it seed into bushland.

name: Diploglottis australis
description: A tall rainforest tree with large glossy leaves and acid, orange-brown fruit that can be made into jam or juice. It needs space and shelter.
edible: The yellow or orange-brown fruit is acidic and refreshing, and is eaten raw or made into jam or juice.
care_note: Please correctly identify and prepare any bush food before eating it.

name: Dipogon lignosus
description: A vigorous twining climber from South Africa with woody stems. It is a serious weed of disturbed bushland, especially near the coast, where it smothers low plants and climbs trees.
care_note: It is a serious bushland weed in NSW, QLD, SA, VIC and WA, so please do not plant it and remove it where it grows.

name: Dracophyllum secundum
description: A shrub to 1 m, lying along the ground or erect, found on sandstone ledges and wet cliff faces and flowering mostly from August to December.

name: Echium plantagineum
description: A hairy winter annual weed with purple flowers in spring, serious in pastures across southern Australia. It sets large amounts of seed that last for years.
care_note: NSW asks everyone to take reasonable steps to prevent and minimise its risk, and it should not be sold in parts of NSW; it is poisonous to livestock and its hairy leaves can irritate skin.

name: Ehrharta erecta
description: A tufted perennial grass from South Africa up to 60 cm high that is a weed of moist, shady sites.
care_note: It is a weed of moist, shady sites in several states, so please do not let it seed.

name: Erica lusitanica
description: An erect shrub from southern Europe, 0.5 to 3.3 m tall, that has escaped from gardens into pastures, scrub and roadsides, mainly in the Blue Mountains.
care_note: PlantNET calls it a garden escape that is locally abundant in the Blue Mountains of NSW, so please avoid planting it near bushland.

name: Erigeron karvinskianus
description: A sprawling perennial 20 to 30 cm high with pale purple daisies that fade to white and pink. It escapes from gardens and rockeries into moist disturbed ground.
care_note: It escapes from gardens and rockeries into moist disturbed ground, so please keep it contained.

name: Erythrina crista-galli
description: A small deciduous tree with thorny stems and scarlet pea flowers in clusters. It has escaped gardens and invades waterways and wetlands in eastern Australia.
care_note: It is listed as council pest vegetation under Brisbane City Council's Natural Asset Local Law, so please do not plant it.

name: Eucalyptus racemosa
description: A tree to about 15 m of dry woodland on shallow sandy soils over sandstone, known for the scribbles on its bark.

name: Euphorbia cyathophora
description: A short-lived upright herb, usually under 1 m, with milky sap and red-based leaves below the flowers. It is an environmental weed of beach dunes and creeks in south-east Queensland and northern NSW.
care_note: It is an environmental weed in Queensland and New South Wales, so please remove it completely rather than leaving cuttings.

name: Eupomatia laurina
description: A dense, spreading evergreen small tree or large shrub with cream, sweetly scented flowers and foliage that turns red-bronze in cool weather. Its soft, guava-like fruit is edible and it can be kept smaller by pruning or growing it in a large pot.
pruning: It responds well to pruning, which keeps it smaller.
edible: The fruit has creamy pulp, is ripe when soft to squeeze, and is eaten raw, made into jam or jelly, or dried and crushed as a flavouring.
care_note: Mulch well and keep the soil moist, in a frost-free spot.

name: Ficus coronata
description: A small tree to 8 m with sandpaper-textured leaves and sweet figs along the trunk and branches. The fruit feeds many birds and flying foxes, and it hosts butterflies.
edible: The figs are sweet and edible.

name: Genista linifolia
description: An evergreen, erect or spreading shrub to 3 m with yellow pea flowers, from the western Mediterranean. It is a Weed of National Significance that invades woodland, dunes and disturbed sites.
care_note: It is a declared weed in the ACT, NSW and VIC; please do not plant it and remove it where it grows. It is believed to be toxic but is rarely grazed.

name: Genista monspessulana
description: A weedy, erect evergreen shrub with bright yellow pea flowers that forms dense thickets and builds a long-lived seedbank. It is a Weed of National Significance.
care_note: It is a declared weed in New South Wales, South Australia, Tasmania and Victoria, so please do not plant it and remove it where it grows.

name: Gomphocarpus physocarpus
description: A South African shrub, 0.5 to 2 m tall, with inflated seed pods that has become common in waste places and on riverbanks in NSW and Queensland.

name: Goodia lotifolia
description: A small to medium, open shrub that is covered in bright yellow pea flowers with a red centre in spring. It is a hardy garden plant.
care_note: It should not be allowed to dry out, and it needs good drainage.

name: Grevillea aquifolium
description: A variable grevillea, from a prostrate scrambler to a shrub 1 to 2 m high, with toothed leaves and red toothbrush flowers. Honeyeaters visit the flowers.
care_note: It resents humidity and can be unreliable in coastal New South Wales and Queensland.

name: Grevillea lavandulacea
description: A variable small shrub, rarely over 1 m, with red spider flowers in its popular Tanunda form. It does best in drier climates.
care_note: Avoid fertilisers containing phosphorus.

name: Gynochthodes jasminoides
description: A woody climber, not vigorous, with fragrant white to purple flowers followed by small orange fruit. It attracts butterflies, birds and bees and suits a hanging basket.

name: Hedychium gardnerianum
description: A large herb with flower stems to 2.5 m and yellow flowers with a red stamen. It spreads by underground stems and forms dense colonies in moist, shaded bushland.
care_note: In Queensland it is Category 3 Restricted Matter under the Biosecurity Act 2014, so it must not be distributed or released, and it is also an environmental weed in NSW.

name: Heliotropium amplexicaule
description: A low perennial herb with purple or lilac flowers with a yellow throat. It is a weed from South America, mostly on roadsides, disturbed sites and pastures.
care_note: It is regarded as an environmental weed in NSW, Queensland and South Australia, and Brisbane City Council lists no declaration for it. Please remove it from your garden.

name: Hydrocotyle laxiflora
description: A creeping perennial herb with round to kidney-shaped leaves and rhizomes over a metre long, often in moist places. Its flower clusters smell unpleasant.

name: Ilex aquifolium
description: A shrub or small tree to 10 m or more with glossy, spiny leaves and bright red berries, grown in cooler areas. It occasionally naturalises in parts of NSW.
care_note: It occasionally naturalises in the Blue Mountains, Southern Highlands and ACT.

name: Imperata cylindrica
description: A tufted perennial grass with stiff, upright leaves and foxtail-like flower heads. It is a host plant for several native butterflies and its leaves were traditionally used to make dilly bags.

name: Isopogon anethifolius
description: An erect shrub, 1 to 3 m tall, that flowers in spring and grows in dry forest and heath on sandstone.

name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
description: A deciduous or semi-evergreen tree with lavender-blue flowers, widely planted for street and garden shade. It has spread from gardens into bushland in south-east Queensland.
care_note: Brisbane City Council lists it as a pest vegetation species, and large trees are very hard to control once established, so think before planting near bushland in Queensland.

name: Lantana montevidensis
description: A low, spreading shrub under 30 cm tall that forms dense thickets and flowers most of the year. It comes from tropical South America and is a weed of wasteland.
care_note: PlantNET calls it a weed of wasteland, so please keep it out of bushland.

name: Leptorhynchos squamatus
description: An erect or ascending herb 10 to 40 cm high that grows in open areas or low grassland at higher altitudes.

name: Leucaena leucocephala
description: A tree 2 to 8 m high with feathery leaves and green to creamy-white flower heads. It is native to Mexico and has naturalised in the tropics and subtropics.
care_note: It is a naturalised weed in Queensland and northern New South Wales, so do not plant it.

name: Leucophyta brownii
description: A dense, rounded little shrub with silvery, hairy stems and small button-like yellowish-white flower heads. Its silver foliage suits coastal and dry sunny gardens, and it needs good drainage.

name: Ligustrum sinense
description: A large shrub or small tree that invades gullies and creeks and forms dense thickets in eastern Australia. Its scented flowers can trigger severe allergies, and birds spread its berries.

toxic.note: Weeds Australia says the leaves and fruit are poisonous to livestock and humans, and the flowers can cause severe allergic reactions.

care_note: Queensland treats it as a category 3 restricted plant, so it is illegal to give away, sell or release it there. It is a declared weed in the ACT, NSW, QLD and WA.

name: Lobelia anceps
description: A small trailing perennial about 30 cm tall with blue to mauve two-lipped flowers in summer and autumn. It likes moist soil and can root along its stems and spread.

name: Lonicera japonica
description: A semi-deciduous climber or scrambler to 7 to 10 m with paired flowers. It is a weed that has naturalised in moist gullies, especially around Sydney.
care_note: It is native to east Asia and naturalises in moist gullies, so avoid planting it near bushland.

name: Lophostemon confertus
description: A tall tree with a dense crown, glossy dark green leaves and white flowers, widely used as a street tree. It provides food and shelter for koalas, gliders and birds.

name: Lycium ferocissimum
description: A dense, spiny shrub to 5 m with small leaves, lilac flowers and shiny red berries. It is an aggressive weed spread by birds.

toxic.note: All parts are poisonous, though the risk is believed to be low.

care_note: A Weed of National Significance, declared in every state and territory except WA; its spines are sharp, so wear heavy gloves and remove it before it fruits.

name: Macaranga tanarius
description: A fast-growing small tree to 6 m with large rounded red-veined leaves and bristly yellow fruit capsules. Its flowers attract lorikeets.

name: Mallotus philippensis
description: A fast-growing, very hardy shade tree to about 18 m with stiff leaves and small red powdery fruit capsules. It suits street planting.

name: Medicago polymorpha
description: A low weedy legume with leaves in threes and coiled, spiny burr-like pods. It is regarded as an environmental weed in Victoria, NSW and WA.
care_note: It is not declared in Queensland, but it is an environmental weed in Victoria, NSW and WA, so please remove it before the burrs set.

name: Myoporum insulare
description: A hardy, spreading evergreen shrub with white flowers, used for coastal hedges, windbreaks and binding sandy soil. It handles salt spray and dry conditions.
care_note: In South Australia it is a risk to sewer pipes, so please plant it at least 3.5 m from any sewer main or pipe.

name: Neolitsea dealbata
description: A tree with long leaves that are grey underneath, rusty or pink new growth and purple-black fruit that birds eat. It is a host plant for several butterflies.

name: Nephrolepis cordifolia
description: A fern with erect or hanging fronds up to 75 cm long and wiry runners that bear tubers, often grown in gardens and indoors. It has escaped and established around Sydney and beyond.
care_note: PlantNET says it has escaped from cultivation and established in the Sydney area and beyond.

name: Olearia ramulosa
description: A small to medium upright shrub with narrow dark green leaves and many small white daisy flowers. It suits screening and low hedges and can grow under existing trees.

name: Oxalis pes-caprae
description: A weedy bulb with clover-like leaves and bright yellow trumpet flowers in winter and spring. It spreads by bulbils in soil and nursery stock and is hard to remove from gardens.
care_note: Declared weed in Victoria only; bulbs and bulbils travel in soil and nursery stock, so do not move soil from infested areas. All parts are high in oxalate and poisonous to stock.

name: Ozothamnus ferrugineus
description: A tall shrub or small tree with cream flower clusters in summer. It suits the back of a garden bed.
care_note: It prefers moist, well-drained soil.

name: Patersonia occidentalis
description: An evergreen, clumping plant with stiff grass-like leaves that grows from an underground rhizome. Each purple-blue flower lasts only a day, but a well-grown clump produces many over the season.

name: Pelargonium australe
description: A small, hairy, herbaceous plant with lobed leaves and white or pink flowers streaked deep red. It suits rockeries and pots and is easy from cuttings.

name: Pelargonium capitatum
description: A bushy sub-shrub to about 60 cm with softly hairy, rose-scented leaves and pink, white or pale purple flowers in summer.
pruning: Remove spent flowers and trim as required.
care_note: It is frost-tender.

name: Pennisetum setaceum
description: A tussock grass about 1 m tall when flowering, with fluffy purple flower spikes. It is an escaped garden plant and a serious weed of roadsides, pastures and bushland.
care_note: It is a declared weed in NSW, Queensland and WA, so please do not plant or dump it, and replace it with a non-weedy grass.

name: Philydrum lanuginosum
description: An upright wetland plant, up to 2 m or more, that grows in swamps and along stream and dam edges and flowers in the warmer months.

name: Phoenix canariensis
description: A slow-growing, large palm with a stout trunk and a crown of up to 100 arching leaves, with orange-yellow dates in summer. It is a big feature palm that suits coastal sites and large gardens.

toxic.note: NC State lists it as non-toxic to cats, dogs and horses. The leaf bases have sharp spines, so wear eye protection when pruning.

edible: The fruit is edible but not flavourful.
care_note: Its leaf bases carry sharp spines, and it can become weedy in parts of Australia.

name: Pittosporum multiflorum
description: A small spiny shrub with small toothed leaves, tubular white flowers and edible orange berries. Its berries feed fruit-eating birds and it hosts the bright copper butterfly.
edible: The orange berries are listed as bush tucker.
care_note: Its branches are spiny.

name: Platylobium formosum
description: A straggly understorey shrub with wiry stems, veined leaves and large bright yellow pea flowers with a red centre. It is hardy in moist, shady sites but is not often grown.
care_note: It needs good drainage.

name: Podolobium ilicifolium
description: A stiff, upright shrub with arching stems, holly-like leaves and yellow pea flowers. Its seed pods feed native birds.

name: Polygala myrtifolia
description: A weedy South African evergreen shrub to about 3 m that seeds freely from gardens into bushland, forming dense stands.
care_note: It is a declared weed in South Australia, so please do not plant it there and remove it where it grows.

name: Portulaca oleracea
description: A low, spreading succulent herb with small yellow flowers that grows as a weed of disturbed and cultivated ground.

name: Pseudognaphalium luteoalbum
description: An erect, woolly grey annual herb with small yellow flower heads in spring and early summer. It is widespread in many soils and communities.

name: Ptilotus polystachyus
description: A perennial herb to 1 m high with long cylindrical yellowish-green flower spikes. It is common in drier inland areas.

name: Raphanus raphanistrum
description: A slender herb 15 to 50 cm high with yellow or white flowers and seed pods that break into one-seeded sections. It is a widespread weed from Europe.
care_note: It is a widespread weed in every state and the Northern Territory.

name: Ricinus communis
description: A large, fast shrub with big glossy lobed leaves and spiny fruit, and a weed along watercourses and neglected ground. All parts, and especially the seeds, are poisonous.

toxic.note: The seeds contain ricin and can be fatal if eaten; sap can cause temporary blindness and the leaves or seeds can cause dermatitis. Wear gloves and eye protection when removing it.

care_note: It is a declared weed in the NT only, but it is poisonous and spreads along watercourses; please remove seedlings, wearing gloves.

name: Rivina humilis
description: A small shrub or woody herb with whitish flower clusters followed by glossy red berries. It prefers damp, shady places and is an environmental weed in Queensland and New South Wales.
care_note: It is an environmental weed in Queensland and NSW and is listed as a Council Pest Vegetation under Brisbane City Council's local law. Please remove it by cutting, spraying or pulling the whole plant.

name: Romulea rosea
description: A weedy cormous plant with tough grooved leaves and small pink, purple or white flowers in spring. It invades lawns and pasture and is hard to remove.
care_note: Declared weed in NSW and WA; pulling often snaps the leaves and leaves the corm behind, and the seed spreads mostly by mowing and dumped garden waste or soil.

name: Rubus rosifolius
description: A shrub with trailing, hairy stems to 2 m long, white flowers most of the year and red fruit at the edges of rainforest and tall forest. The fruit is edible but bland.
edible: The red fruit is edible but insipid.

name: Santalum acuminatum
description: A large shrub or small tree of semi-arid country with greyish-green leaves and sweet-sour fruit used in jams and chutneys. It lives partly off a host plant's roots.
edible: The fruit is a bush food used in jams and chutneys.
care_note: Young plants must not be allowed to dry out.

name: Scabiosa atropurpurea
description: An erect herb up to 60 cm with pincushion-like heads from dark purple to white, grown as an ornamental. It sometimes naturalises.

name: Scaevola calendulacea
description: A spreading, mat-forming scrambling plant of coastal dunes with fan-shaped blue flowers. It is a low groundcover to about 40 cm high.

name: Schinus areira
description: A large, spreading evergreen tree with red panicles of flowers, traditionally planted around homesteads and in parks for shade. It tolerates drought and difficult sites.
care_note: Its roots can be invasive, so please plant it away from buildings, and it needs protection from strong wind.

name: Senecio linearifolius
description: A perennial herb or shrub 50 to 150 cm tall that flowers throughout the year, mostly in wet sclerophyll forest.

name: Senecio quadridentatus
description: An upright, cobwebby-white perennial herb with narrow leaves and narrow yellow flower heads, common on disturbed ground especially after fire.

name: Senna pendula
description: A fast-growing, sprawling weedy shrub with bright yellow flowers and long hanging pods. It invades gardens, waterways and bushland.
care_note: Declared weed in NSW and WA, and a Pest Vegetation under Brisbane City Council's local law; remove it before it seeds.

name: Solanum americanum
description: A spreading herb or short-lived shrub up to 1.3 m with white flowers and purple-black berries that flowers most of the year, a cosmopolitan weed of disturbed ground.

name: Solanum aviculare
description: An erect shrub to 4 m with summer flowers that grows in disturbed ground and coastal rainforest. Some NSW plants are probably naturalised from gardens.

name: Solanum seaforthianum
description: A sprawling environmental weed vine with deeply lobed leaves, mauve-blue star flowers and bright red berries. Birds spread it into bushland.

toxic.note: Leaves, stems and unripe fruit are poisonous; eating them can cause stomach upset. In NSW call the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26.

care_note: In NSW it is a pest plant under the general biosecurity duty, so please pull seedlings before it fruits and remove all fruit.

name: Spathodea campanulata
description: A large tree with orange-red tulip-shaped flowers in clusters. It is a significant environmental weed in Queensland and the Northern Territory.
care_note: It is a Category 3 Restricted Matter under Queensland's Biosecurity Act 2014 and must not be distributed or disposed of; it is toxic to native stingless bees.

name: Spyridium parvifolium
description: A spreading shrub with dark green oval to round leaves and flat clusters of tiny white flowers. It suits cottage gardens, low screens and shaded understorey planting.
pruning: It responds well to regular tip pruning to keep its shape.

name: Stylidium armeria
description: A perennial herb with a basal tuft of narrow leaves and many-flowered upright spikes, with the trigger flowers typical of its genus.

name: Stylidium graminifolium
description: A tufted, grass-like plant with pink flowers on stalks up to 40 cm, whose trigger springs when an insect lands and dusts it with pollen. It suits pots and is hardier than most trigger plants.

name: Suaeda australis
description: A hairless, spreading perennial with fleshy leaves, about 1 m tall, found on coastal and estuary shores and in salt marshes.

name: Tabernaemontana pandacaqui
description: A shrub to 3 m that flowers in spring and summer and grows in warmer rainforest on the NSW north coast and in Queensland.

name: Tecoma stans
description: A densely branched shrub or small tree, 3 to 8 m tall, with yellow trumpet flowers through the year. It has escaped from gardens and is a weed in tropical and subtropical Australia.
care_note: It is a declared weed in NSW, Queensland and WA, so please do not plant it, and pull small plants out before they seed.

name: Templetonia retusa
description: A hardy shrub 1 to 2 m high with greyish leaves and large deep red pea flowers, also white or yellow, that attract honeyeaters. It has proved reliable in humid eastern climates.
care_note: It needs well-drained soil.

name: Thunbergia alata
description: A twining vine with orange or yellow tubular flowers that have a black throat. It is an environmental weed in New South Wales and Queensland, where it can escape into bushland.
care_note: It is an environmental weed in NSW and Queensland and is listed as a Council Pest Vegetation under Brisbane City Council's local law. Please remove it completely and do not let it spread into bushland.

name: Tillandsia usneoides
description: A rootless epiphyte that hangs in grey, moss-like strands from trees or wooden supports. It needs high humidity and clean air.
care_note: Prune it if it becomes too heavy for its host, and it needs no watering outdoors where the air is humid.

name: Toona ciliata
description: A large, spreading deciduous rainforest tree with a straight trunk and scaly bark. It suits large properties with deep, moist soil.
care_note: Cedar tip moth can damage new growth, which often leaves a smaller tree with several trunks.

name: Ulex europaeus
description: A dense, spiny, woody shrub of 1 to 3 m (up to 7 m) with yellow flowers in spring and autumn. It is a serious weed in Tasmania, Victoria and South Australia.
care_note: It is a Weed of National Significance and declared in all states and territories. Do not plant it, and avoid spraying when it is in flower or bees are active.

name: Verbascum thapsus
description: A tall, grey, woolly biennial that forms a rosette in its first year and a single yellow flower spike in its second. It is a weed in Australia.
care_note: It is a noxious weed in Victoria and New South Wales; please do not plant it, and note that its dense hairs irritate skin.

name: Vinca major
description: A trailing evergreen groundcover with glossy leaves and blue to violet flowers. It is an environmental weed that spreads by rooting stems and smothers native plants.
care_note: Declared in the ACT, and NSW asks people not to buy, sell or release it; it is poisonous to livestock, so dispose of cuttings carefully.

name: Viola betonicifolia
description: A tufted little herb with arrowhead-shaped leaves and pale purple to violet flowers, mostly in spring. It suits rockeries, small gardens and pots, and self-sows without becoming invasive.

name: Viola odorata
description: A perennial herb with heart-shaped leaves, slender runners and fragrant deep violet flowers. It is widely grown in gardens and occasionally naturalises.
care_note: It is introduced from Europe and occasionally naturalises.

name: Watsonia meriana
description: An erect clumping herb to 2.5 m with sword-shaped leaves and orange trumpet flowers from late October. It spreads by corms and bulbils and is a major weed along rivers and roadsides.
care_note: It is a declared weed in South Australia and Victoria, so please do not plant it or dump garden refuse containing bulbils. It is suspected of being poisonous to livestock.

name: Wikstroemia indica
description: A shrub or small tree, up to 4 m, with tough stringy bark once used as cord, found in forest, shrubland and along streams on the NSW coast.

toxic.note: The Lucid key for south-eastern NSW says the fruit and leaves are poisonous.

name: Xanthorrhoea semiplana
description: A very slow-growing grass tree with a trunk topped by a tuft of grass-like leaves and cream flower spikes. It suits pots and sunny, well-drained spots.
care_note: It needs good drainage and is susceptible to the root rot Phytophthora cinnamomi.
